**Translation:**

﴿Then if it becomes known﴾ (fa-in ʿuthira), i.e., if it is discovered ﴿that the two had incurred sin﴾ — by an act that made sin obligatory for them and made them deserving of being described as "truly among the sinners" — ﴿then two others﴾ (fa-ākharān), i.e., two other witnesses ﴿shall stand in their place, from among those against whom [the sin] was incurred﴾. That is: ﴿from among those against whom [the sin] was incurred﴾, meaning from among those who were wronged, namely the family of the deceased and his kinsmen. In the story of Badil: when the treachery of the two men became evident, two men from among his heirs swore that the cup belonged to their companion, and that their testimony was more worthy than the testimony of the two [others].

﴿The nearest [in kinship]﴾ (al-awlayān) — the most entitled to testify by reason of their kinship to them, or by reason of their knowledge of them. Its nominative case: it is read as "al-awwalayān" as though it were said, "And who are they?" and the answer was "al-awlayān," or it is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "yaqūmān," or for "ākharān." (Those against whom the nearest [in kinship] [had a right]) — Ḥafṣ [reads it thus]. That is: "from" the heirs ﴿who were [the ones] against whom the nearest [in kinship] had the right﴾, from among them, by testimony, that they should single them out for standing as witnesses, and that they should, through them, expose the lying of the liars.

(al-awwalīn) — Ḥamzah and Abū Bakr [read it thus], as an attribute of "alladhīna" in the genitive case, or in the accusative case by way of praise. They were called "awwalīn" (first) because they were mentioned first in His saying: ﴿The testimony between you﴾.

﴿They swear by God: "Our testimony is more worthy than their testimony"﴾ — that is, our oath is more worthy of acceptance than the oath of these two treacherous executors. ﴿And we have not transgressed﴾ — and we have not exceeded the truth in our oath. ﴿Indeed we, then, would be among the wrongdoers﴾ — that is, if we swore falsely.

﴿That﴾, the ruling just mentioned, ﴿is closer﴾, meaning more likely, ﴿that they will bring﴾, that is, the witnesses in cases like that incident, ﴿the testimony (shahada, witness testimony) in its proper form﴾, as they bore it, without any betrayal in it. ﴿Or they will fear that oaths (yamin, oaths) will be returned after their oaths﴾, meaning that the oaths of other witnesses will be repeated after theirs, so that they will be disgraced by the exposure of their lying. ﴿And fear God﴾ regarding betrayal and the false oath. ﴿And listen﴾ with the listening of acceptance and response. ﴿And God does not guide the defiant people﴾, those who depart from obedience.

If you ask: what is the meaning of "or" (aw) here? I say: its meaning is that this is closer to their bringing the testimony with truth and sincerity, either for the sake of God, or out of fear of shame and disgrace through the return of oaths. Those who hold that the oath is returned to the claimant (radd al-yamin, returning the oath) have used this as evidence. The answer is that the heirs had claimed against the two Christians that they had betrayed, so they swore. When their lying became apparent, they claimed that they had sold the items they had concealed, and the heirs denied this. So the oath fell upon the heirs because of their denial of the sale.

﴿Yawma﴾ (the day) is in the accusative, governed by ﴿udhkurū﴾ (remember) or ﴿aḥdharū﴾ (beware). ﴿Yajma'u Allāhu al-rusula fa-yaqūlu mādhā ujibtum﴾ (On the day when God gathers the messengers and says, "What answer were you given?"): that is, what your peoples replied to you when you called them to faith. This question is a rebuke to those who denied them. ﴿Mādhā﴾ is in the accusative, governed by ﴿ujibtum﴾, in the manner of the accusative of the verbal noun (naṣb al-maṣdar), meaning: "What kind of answer were you given?" ﴿Qālū lā 'ilma lanā﴾ (They will say, "We have no knowledge") of the sincerity of our people. Its evidence is ﴿Innaka anta 'allāmu al-ghuyūb﴾ (Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen). Or (they have no knowledge) of what they introduced after us; its evidence is ﴿Kunta anta al-raqība 'alayhim﴾ (You were the Watcher over them) [al-Mā'ida: 117]. Or they said this out of courtesy (ta'addaban), meaning: our knowledge is insignificant in comparison with Your knowledge, and is submerged in it, so it is as though we have no knowledge.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 110:**

﴿When Allah said﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, or apposition, glossed as a restatement of the preceding noun) for "the Day when He gathers" (*yawma yajmaʿu*). ﴿O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother,﴾ in that I purified her and chose her above the women of the worlds. The governing element (*al-ʿāmil*) in ﴿when I strengthened you﴾ (*idh ayyadtuka*), meaning "I empowered you," is ﴿My favour﴾ (*niʿmatī*). ﴿With the Holy Spirit﴾ refers to Jibril, peace be upon him, by whom he was strengthened so that the proof would be established against them, or it refers to the word by which religion is given life. He was attributed to *al-Quds* (the Holy), because he is the cause of purity from the filth of sins. Its proof is ﴿you speak to the people in the cradle﴾, which is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial accusative, glossed as a state or condition of the subject) meaning: you speak to them as a child, as a miracle, ﴿and in maturity﴾, as a means of conveying the message. ﴿When I taught you﴾ is conjoined (*maʿtūf*) to ﴿when I strengthened you﴾, and similarly ﴿when you create﴾, ﴿when you bring forth﴾, ﴿when I restrained﴾, ﴿when I inspired﴾. ﴿The Book﴾ means the writing (*al-khaṭṭ*), ﴿and the Wisdom﴾ means the firm and correct speech, ﴿and the Torah and the Gospel.﴾ ﴿When you create﴾ means you determine, ﴿from clay, the likeness of a bird﴾, a form resembling the form of a bird, ﴿by My permission﴾, by My facilitation.

﴿Then you breathe into it﴾: the pronoun refers to the *kāf* (the "you" of the address), because it is the description of the form which Jesus used to create and into which he breathed. It does not refer to the form mentioned as its antecedent, because that is not of his creation. Likewise the pronoun in ﴿and it becomes a bird by My permission﴾. ﴿And you heal the blind and the leper by My permission﴾ is conjoined to ﴿you create﴾. ﴿And when you bring forth the dead﴾ from the graves, alive, ﴿by My permission﴾. It has been said that he brought forth Sam son of Noah, two men, a woman, and a girl.

﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you﴾, that is, the Jews, when they resolved to kill him, ﴿when you came to them﴾ is an adverbial of time (*ẓarf*, glossed as a temporal complement) governed by ﴿I restrained﴾, ﴿with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said, "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾ (*sāḥirun*, "magician"): Ḥamzah and ʿAlī read it as *sāḥirun*.

(p-485)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 111:

﴿And when I inspired (awhaytu)﴾ — i.e., I inspired into the heart (alhamtu) — ﴿the disciples (al-Hawariyyin)﴾ — the select companions (al-Khawass), or the chosen ones (al-Asfiya') — ﴿that you believe﴾ — i.e., believe ﴿in Me and My Messenger.﴾ They said: ﴿We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾ — i.e., bear witness that we are sincere (mukhlisun), from aslama wajhahu (he submitted his face, i.e., devoted himself wholly).

﴿When the disciples said﴾, meaning: remember when the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said, ﴿"O ʿIsa, son of Maryam"﴾. "ʿIsa" is in the accusative (nasb), following the vowel of "ibn" (حَرَكَةَ الِابْنِ), as in the phrase "yā Zayda ibna ʿAmr."

﴿Is your Lord able﴾ means: does He do it? Or: will your Lord give you if you ask Him? "Istaṭāʿa" and "aṭāʿa" have the same meaning, like "istajāba" and "ajāba."

(Is your Lord able): ʿAli reads "hal tastaṭīʿu rabbaka" (with the verb in the second person and "rabbaka" in the accusative). Meaning: are you able to ask your Lord? The genitive noun has been omitted, so the sense is: will you ask Him, without anything preventing you from asking Him?

﴿to send down upon us﴾: "yunazzila" (with the verb in the third person) is read by Makki and Basri.

﴿a table spread from heaven﴾: "māʾida" is the food-laden table (al-khiwān) when food is on it, from "māda" meaning "he gave," as if it sways (tamīdu) toward whoever approaches it.

﴿He said: "Fear God"﴾ regarding the demand for signs after the miracles have appeared. ﴿"If you are believers"﴾, since faith necessitates piety (taqwā).

They said, "We want to eat from it" (﴿قالُوا نُرِيدُ أنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنها﴾) for blessing (tabarruk, seeking blessing), "and that our hearts may be assured" (﴿وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنا﴾), and that we may increase in certainty (yaqin), like the saying of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): "But so that my heart may be assured" (﴿وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾) [al-Baqarah: 260]. "And that we may know that you have told us the truth" (﴿وَنَعْلَمَ أنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنا﴾), meaning: we may know your truthfulness by direct witness, as we knew it by inference (istidlal, reasoning from evidence). "And that we may be among its witnesses" (﴿وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْها مِنَ الشاهِدِينَ﴾) by what we witnessed, for those who come after us.

Since the question was for the increase of knowledge and not for testing (God), ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O Allah"﴾ (p-486) its original form is "Yā Allāh," so "yā" was dropped and the "mīm" was substituted for it. ﴿"Our Lord"﴾ is a second vocative. ﴿"Send down to us a table (spread with food) from heaven, which will be a festival for us"﴾, i.e., the day of its descent will be a festival. It was said: it was the day of Sunday, and for this reason the Christians took it as a festival. Or "ʿīd" means a returning joy, and for this reason one says "a day of ʿīd" (yawm ʿīd), so its meaning is: it will be a source of joy and happiness for us. ﴿"For the first of us and the last of us"﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "for us," with the governing verb repeated, i.e., for those of our time among the people of our religion, and for those who will come after us; or the last of the people will eat from it as the first of them eats; or for those who came before us and those who follow. ﴿"And a sign from You"﴾ as evidence of the soundness of my prophethood. Then he emphasized this by his saying: ﴿"And provide for us, and You are the best of providers"﴾, i.e., give us what we have asked of You, for You are the best of givers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 115:

﴿Allah said: "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."﴾

115 (Allah said: "Indeed I will send it down to you") With the doubled letter (tashdid) on the nun (munazziluha): Medinan, Shami and ʿAsim (readings). He promised the sending down, and He stipulated a condition upon them with His words: ﴿whoever disbelieves after that among you﴾, after its being sent down, ﴿then I will surely punish him with a punishment﴾, i.e., a punishment (taʿdhib), like salam meaning taslim (greeting). The pronoun in "lā uʿadhdhibuhu" (I will not punish him) refers to the verbal noun (masdar). If by "adhab" (punishment) is meant that with which one is punished, there would have been a necessity for the preposition bi (with). ﴿with a punishment with which I will not punish anyone among the worlds﴾. From al-Hasan: the table (al-ma'idah) did not come down; and if it had come down, it would have been a festival until the Day of Resurrection, due to His saying: "and for the last of us" (wa-akhirina). The correct view is that it did come down. From Wahb: a table came down, inverted, carried by the angels; upon it was every food except meat. It was said: they would find on it whatever they wished. It was also said: it would descend wherever they were, in the morning and in the evening.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 116:

﴿And when Allah says: "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"﴾ The majority (al-jumhur) hold that this question will be put on the Day of Resurrection; its evidence is the context (siyaq) and the sequence (sibaq) of the verse. It has also been said that He addressed him with this when He raised him up to heaven; its evidence is the word "idh" (when). ﴿He said: "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say"﴾ — glory be to You, [exalted] above having any partner — ﴿"It is not for me"﴾ — it is not fitting for me — ﴿"to say what I have no right to say"﴾ — to say a statement that it is not right for me to make. ﴿"If I had said it, You would surely have known it"﴾ — if it be true that I said it in the past, then You would have known it. The meaning is: I have no need to make an excuse, because You know that I did not say it; and had I said it, You would have known it, because ﴿You know what is in my self﴾ — my essence — ﴿and I do not know what is in Yours﴾ — Your essence. The "self" (nafs) of a thing is its essence and its reality (huwiyyah). The meaning is: You know what I know, and I do not know what You know. ﴿Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen⁠﴾ — this is a confirmation of both sentences together, because what souls harbour is among the unseen things, and because the knowledge of the Knower of the unseen does not reach the knowledge of anyone.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 117:

﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ That is: I did not command them except with what You commanded me. Then he explained what he was commanded, saying: ﴿"Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ Here "an" (that) is explanatory (mufassirah), meaning: "i.e." ﴿And I was a witness over them﴾, a watcher (raqib), ﴿while I was among them﴾, for the duration of my being among them. ﴿But when You took me up (tawaffaytani), You were the Watcher over them﴾, the Guardian (al-Hafiz), ﴿and You are a Witness over all things﴾, of my words and my deeds, and of their words and their deeds.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 5, verse 118:

﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ Al-Zajjaj (Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj) said: Jesus, peace be upon him, knew that among them were those who believed and those who persisted in disbelief, so he said, referring to them all: ﴿If You punish them﴾, that is: if You punish those among them who disbelieved, ﴿then indeed they are Your servants﴾, whom You know to be deniers of Your signs and deniers of Your prophets, and You are just in that, for they disbelieved after the proof had been established against them. ﴿And if You forgive them﴾, that is: those among them who gave up (disbelief) and believed, for that is Your grace, ﴿and You are the Almighty﴾, none can prevent You from what You will, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in that. Or "al-Aziz" means the Strong, the Able to reward; "al-Hakim" means He does not punish except for a wise purpose and a right end.

Allah said: "This is a day when their truthfulness will benefit those who were truthful." Reading al-yawmu in the nominative with the genitive construction (idafa), the phrase is the predicate (khabar) of "hadha" (this): that is, Allah the Exalted says, "This is a day when the truthfulness of the truthful benefits them, their truthfulness being constant in their worldly life and their Hereafter." The sentence formed from the subject and predicate is in a position of accusative (naṣb) as the object of speech (maf'uliyya), just as you say: "Zayd said: 'Amr is departing'." With the accusative, Nafi' reads al-yawma as an adverb of time (zarf), meaning: Allah said this to Jesus, peace be upon him: "A day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful," and it is the Day of Resurrection. "For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them" for their striving that was thanked, "and they are pleased with Him" for the abundant reward. "That is the great triumph" because it is lasting, unlike success in this world, which is not lasting.

For God is the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. [He] exalted Himself above what the Christians said: that with Him there is another god. ﴿And He is over all things Competent﴾, from withholding, giving, bringing into existence, and bringing to an end.

We ask Him to grant us success in what pleases Him, and to make us among those who triumph with His gardens. And may God send blessings upon our master Muhammad, his family, and his companions, and grant them peace.
